claims.title: The transpose-compatible metric cubic family on the real paired lepton carrier has four projective Kantor rays
claims.claim: For V_abc(x,y,z)=a x<y,z>+b z<y,x>+c y<x,z>, the Kantor identities are equivalent to c(c+a)=0 and 3b^2-3ab-ac+bc=0, with nonzero real projective rays (1,0,0), (1,1,0), (1,1,-1), and (3,1,-3).
claims.scope: Real two-dimensional lepton carrier; metric-built cubic products; transpose-paired rectangular realization.
falsifiers: A basis instance violating either Kantor identity on one of the four rays.
A nonzero real projective solution outside the four algebraic components.

claims.title: One paired Kantor ray simultaneously has CP covariance, nonzero contact layer, and the established Jordan shadow
claims.claim: The ray V(x,y,z)=x<y,z>, represented on paired rectangles by transpose-reversed six-word coefficients (1/2,1/2,-1/2), is a Kantor triple product, has K nonzero, is transpose covariant, and outer-symmetrizes to the established Hermitian Jordan triple.
claims.scope: Real paired lepton rectangles only; no claim yet about the complex full Furey carrier or a microscopic action.
falsifiers: Failure of matrix-level transpose covariance.
Failure of either Kantor identity.
Mismatch between outer symmetrization and the existing Jordan triple.

claims.title: The paired six-word Kantor completion is a physical Standard-Model/Furey product
claims.claim: The distinguished real product does not extend as a Kantor system to the phase-doubled complex Furey lepton pair within the complete real-coefficient dagger-built metric family; both real rays with nonzero K fail the Kantor identities.
falsifiers: A nonzero-K coefficient ray in the stated dagger-built family that passes both phase-doubled Kantor identities.
An error in either preserved explicit basis counterexample.

claims.title: Positive Freudenthal inverse pairs are dual-GL(2) orbits labelled by lambda
claims.claim: For N_+={(A,lambda A^-1):A>0,lambda>0}, the dual GL(2) action is transitive at fixed lambda and N_+/GL(2) is isomorphic to the positive real line, with lambda=tr(AC)/2=sqrt(det(A)det(C)).
falsifiers: Two positive inverse pairs with the same lambda that are not related by dual congruence.
Failure of lambda invariance under the dual action.

claims.title: Freudenthal quartic/triple criticality does not select scale, embedding line, or orientation
claims.claim: The restricted quartic and cubic map vanish for every positive lambda on the inverse locus, while norm symmetry moves the octonionic link line and contains its orientation reversal; these invariants therefore cannot select lambda, the embedding line, or its sign.
falsifiers: A scalar internal to the same invariant structure that varies along the lambda quotient without extra scale data.
A restricted invariant distinguishing two norm-related link lines.

claims.title: A Gaussian/log-determinant action can choose lambda but Freudenthal symmetry alone cannot
claims.claim: The stationary equation of tr(AC)-kappa log det C is C=kappa A^-1, so a state or normalization supplies lambda; a pure function of the restricted Freudenthal quartic is stationary along every inverse ray and supplies no lambda potential.
falsifiers: A variation error in the log-determinant action.
A pure quartic action whose derivative is nonzero along the critical-null inverse locus.

claims.title: A physical Higgs, Majorana, boundary, or CP-breaking datum selects the real Kantor carrier
claims.claim: An independently derived Standard-Model datum may select the real subbundle on which the CP-compatible contact Kantor product exists, without choosing a basis or erasing the global orientation witness.
falsifiers: Every available physical real structure either violates gauge covariance or leaves a continuous family of real slices.
The selected slice makes the local K generator unobservable or unrelated to the global orientation-odd channel.

claims.title: A gauge-covariant real selector is an antiunitary fixed form commuting with the gauge action
claims.claim: For an antiunitary involution J on a complex gauge module, Fix(J) is a gauge-covariant real form iff J commutes with the gauge representation. A two-real-dimensional fixed form with invariant Euclidean metric supports the contact Kantor product x<y,z> and grading (1,2,4,2,1).
falsifiers: A gauge transformation carrying Fix(J) outside itself despite [J,rho(g)]=0.
A failure of either Kantor identity on the fixed Euclidean two-plane.

claims.title: No nonzero linear gauge intertwiner connects a charged Nambu plane to a neutral boundary plane
claims.claim: If the Nambu fixed plane carries R(q theta) with q nonzero and the boundary plane is gauge trivial, S R(q theta)=S for all theta implies S J=0 and hence S=0.
falsifiers: A nonzero 2x2 matrix satisfying S R(q theta)=S for all theta with q nonzero.

claims.title: Matched rotation and reflection reduce Nambu-boundary isometries to signs
claims.claim: When source and boundary retain the same SO(2) connection, metric intertwiners form U(1); matching the real reflection D reduces them to plus or minus I, or plus or minus D when rotation orientation is reversed.
falsifiers: A reflection-compatible orthogonal rotation intertwiner outside the four stated sign classes.

claims.title: The minimal neutral observable escape is a quadratic two-face Gram map with a separate orientation line
claims.claim: One charged complex mode has only one independent quadratic norm coordinate; two equal-charge faces are minimally required to produce a Hermitian Gram carrier, whose phase-aligned slice is H_2(R). The Gram carrier forgets the contact-area sign, which must survive as separate boundary, Pfaffian, or interference data.
falsifiers: A one-mode gauge-invariant quadratic construction with a two-real-dimensional oriented carrier.
Failure of common phase alignment for every candidate pair of Higgs-dressed faces.
Proof that every attached orientation line is gauge or basis artefact.

claims.title: The contact-area orientation is exactly blind to the B-L shear
claims.claim: The incidence shear T_c=[[1,0],[c,1]] fixes the B-L axis, has determinant one, and preserves the two-dimensional contact area form. Since all Yukawa-divergence covectors also annihilate B-L, divergence plus contact orientation cannot determine c.
falsifiers: A value of c for which T_c fails to preserve the area form.
A declared Yukawa-divergence coordinate with nonzero B-L component in the same Dirac branch.

claims.title: Charged-lepton divergence selects the incidence fork but not its B-L-shear representative
claims.claim: The deduplicated and multiplicity incidence coordinates differ first in the charged-lepton channel, 2 versus 4, while every shift by B-L leaves both values unchanged.
falsifiers: Equality of the charged-lepton divergence coordinates after using the declared incidence definitions.
A nonzero Yukawa divergence for completed B-L.

claims.title: The action-derived QFT Gram fixes a unique B-L-orthogonal incidence representative inside each fork
claims.claim: The Grams [[231,9],[9,48]] and [[239,15],[15,48]] select lambda_d-(3/16)q and lambda_m-(5/16)q respectively, with norms 3669/16 and 3749/16.
falsifiers: Non-orthogonality of either displayed representative to q in its stated Gram.
Failure of the Gram to define the physical common source bilinear over the matching window.

claims.title: Topology Gram plus contact area retains an SO(2) frame torsor
claims.claim: An oriented positive two-plane specified only by its metric and area form has SO(2) automorphism group. It therefore cannot canonically identify one topology direction with B-L or incidence.
falsifiers: A nonzero vector or covector constructed equivariantly from a two-dimensional positive metric and compatible area form alone.
Triviality of the exhibited quarter-turn stabilizer.

claims.title: One topology-to-source anchor completes the two-dimensional frame matching
claims.claim: After charged leptons choose the incidence fork and the QFT Gram fixes its B-L-orthogonal representative, one oriented topology vector or covector mapped to a named source axis removes the residual SO(2) torsor; an unoriented line leaves only a common sign.
falsifiers: A residual continuous stabilizer after an oriented unit anchor is fixed.
Proof that every candidate Furey/Higgs/boundary anchor is basis dependent or gauge variant.

claims.title: Minimal local source consistency gives paired admission or paired rejection of the incidence rays
claims.claim: For linear real Standard-Model current sources, locality and Hermiticity admit both incidence rays; derivative-ALP shift symmetry admits both; exact anomaly-free gauging without extra completion data rejects both; and closure under the smallest exact shared-field RG block rejects both. None of these principles selects exactly one ray.
falsifiers: A source-consistency condition within the declared class that is satisfied by exactly one of lambda_d and lambda_m.
A calculation showing that exactly one incidence Yukawa vector is an eigenvector of the declared shared-field block.
An anomaly-free exact gauging of exactly one ray without additional matter, spurions or Wess-Zumino completion data.

claims.title: Anomaly coordinates distinguish the electron fork but do not independently select it
claims.claim: The two incidence rays have anomaly images (16,16,336,51) and (16,16,408,53). Their A3 and A2 entries agree, while the AYY and gravitational differences are fixed by the differing charged-lepton Yukawa coordinate through exact row identities; anomaly data therefore read the fork but supply no independent accept/reject selector.
falsifiers: Failure of either stated anomaly image under the declared rows.
Independence of AYY or Agrav from the five-coordinate Yukawa-plus-A2 quotient.
A completion-independent anomaly criterion accepting exactly one incidence ray.

claims.title: The smallest falsifiable source realization is a discrete two-ray ALP benchmark
claims.claim: With no independent UV gauge operators or fermion-current coefficients, a single derivative ALP coupled at the matching scale to either lambda_d or lambda_m gives a two-hypothesis, one-overall-scale benchmark. The electron chirality amplitude ratio is two and its isolated leading squared-rate ratio is four, while the common quark and weak-anomaly coordinates provide production anchors.
falsifiers: A reconstructed UV vector inconsistent with both projective coordinate sets (10,6,2,1;16) and (10,6,4,1;16).
Necessity of independent UV gauge operators or additional fermion-current directions in the claimed restricted model.
Failure of the isolated equal-kinematics lepton partial width to scale quadratically with the chirality-changing coefficient.

claims.title: Furey electron topology fixes a response channel but no source normalization
claims.claim: The unique electron cycle and named Peirce data identify the charged-lepton response line, but the existing construction contains no independently normalized topology-to-current metric that chooses sector-deduplicated weight one over incidence-multiplicity weight three. A normalized electron-to-quark intertwiner remains the missing selector.
falsifiers: An existing derived Furey pairing that canonically fixes the electron-to-quark response ratio to exactly one of the two incidence values.
A proof that one incidence weighting violates a topology automorphism or a declared normalized state pairing while the other does not.
